payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to 80% capacity; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The cell’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, and its projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Thalliline precipitation requires cycling to be suspended below 4 °C.
